title: OFFSET vs INDEX: same tricks, very different cost
meta_desc: OFFSET vs INDEX for dynamic ranges: volatility and recalculation cost, dependency tracking, when OFFSET is genuinely needed. Verified across all three apps.
intro: Both can build references that move and resize — the difference is that OFFSET is VOLATILE: it recalculates on every change anywhere in the workbook, and everything downstream of it recalculates too. INDEX does most of the same jobs without that tax, which is why 'replace OFFSET with INDEX' is a standard performance fix for slow sheets.

cols: A cell value — or a range when used as INDEX(rng,0,col) / range-end syntax
Yes — plus everything that depends on it
No — recalcs only when its inputs change
Opaque — audit tools can't see what it points at
Universal (both verified in every version of all three apps we test)

when.use_when: Small sheets where its compact height/width arguments read clearly (rolling windows, resizable named ranges) and the volatility cost is negligible.

Anything large or shared: the INDEX:INDEX range trick covers dynamic windows without volatile recalcs, keeps dependency tracing intact, and — combined with MATCH or with modern TAKE/DROP — replaces nearly every OFFSET construction.

compat_note: Both execute identically in every version of Excel, Google Sheets, and LibreOffice we test, including OFFSET's height/width resizing and the INDEX:INDEX range syntax. The volatility difference is also cross-app: all three engines treat OFFSET (and INDIRECT) as volatile.
